points: An SLO says how good a service must be, and the gap it leaves is an error budget for failure and release risk.
Averages hide slow tails, so latency is judged by percentiles: a typical 50 ms request with 5% of requests 20 times slower looks fine on a mean.
Alerts work best on burn rate: a fast burn pages, a slow one opens a ticket, and a short window lets the alert reset.
Tracing every request costs too much, so Dapper and Canopy sample, using a target rate of traces and a token bucket to cap volume.
These alerts and traces feed the earlier reliability topics, such as load shedding, rate limits, circuit breakers and safe rollouts.

A total outage empties a 99.9% budget over 30 days in 43 minutes

prerequisiteReasons.overload-and-cascading-failures: Overload and cascading failures are what these signals have to catch early, so seeing how a system fails comes before measuring whether it is failing.
